Sit down kids and let me tell you a tale, about a reasonable man driven to do unreasonable things.

If I remember right, he bought a piece of stranded real property. He bought the right to occupy the land but cheaped out and did not buy any roads or other access to the land. Probably he just looked at the existing ruts on other people's property and assumed he magically had the right to keep using them forever.

Well that's not how land ownership works. You also have to negotiate and buy access easements (the right to travel across the surface of adjoining land), and utility easements (the right to place aerial wires and subsurface pipelines). If you want to extract the ores and petroleum and turn them into something useful, you have to buy the mineral rights. If you want to fly an aircraft out at low altitude, you have to buy aviation easements.

You can even buy air easements to obtain the prevailing winds, and view easements to secure the right to see local landmarks.

What you cannot do is buy a chunk of land and get any access you want. Unless you buy from a property developer who platted the utilities and roads, you are in for a world of hurt.

Seriously, if you are an American, think of a recent housing development you have seen. Go to the county clerk's website and do a land search for the housing development. You will find a "plat", a record of how the land was subdivided. The plat will include utility easements (powerlines and pipes), streets that have been given to the town for public travel by anyone, public parks, and so forth.

As far as I can tell, this poor "Killdozer" man just couldn't cope with the bureaucracy. I expect he could have gotten everything at an affordable price in the open market, but only knew how to fight. It's a sad tale of an original wild human beating himself to death against the structures of civilization.
